summary: Isolated, bit-exact replacement of a serial ~393-419 us align at first_turn (verified in 07a069 profile) plus 17/71 us at turn_1/turn_4 on the rega path; first_turn carries 186 of 310 shape weight, so a ~2-3% headline gain is plausible and attribution is readable straight from the align kernel rows. No companion is worth one of the 2 remaining checks.
justification: Profile 07a069bc69ba42a8 confirms _align_parallel_kernel at 17.1/16.7 us (turn_1), 71.2/69.6 us (turn_4), 393.9/392.5/396.1/418.9 us (first_turn, 2.1-3.3%), and the prepare log shows 441-454 us eager at T=16384. The mechanism is structural: 33 programs each stream all n=131072 ids twice with a [512x32] compare, so time scales with n on 33 SMs; the two-phase form reads each id ~twice in total over 128-256 programs per launch. The align sits serially between the router join and the rega gather/GEMMs (sorted_ids/block_experts feed them), so saved us become wall-time. Outputs are torch.equal to master's align, so rega GEMM rows should not move. Directions match TASK weights: first_turn ~-350 us/shape on 11.7-19.2 ms is ~2-3% on 186/310 of the weight, against a noise of ~1.5%. That is likely, but not certain, to clear the CI. Weakest links: (1) the ft-class cost of align2 is unmeasured. At T=16384 the place kernel holds a [NCH_P2=128-256, 32] count table plus a [CHUNK, 32] one-hot cumsum per program (128 regs/thread of one-hot at CHUNK 1024, so possible spills), and one tail CTA writes ~115k sentinels plus 33 [256x32] block_experts iterations. My estimate is 15-40 us, not the 30-60 us stated, so the risk is low but real. (2) The turn_1/turn_4 expectations rest on d792, where only sliding turn_4 moved (+4%, which is more than a 55 us saving can explain, so partly noise), turn_1 was flat, and the headline 1.3369 was within CI of its 1.3275 base. Read the turn rows as align-kernel rows, not headline deltas.
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128 (parent): created the ft call site that put _align_parallel on T=16384. Its ft gate (rega 3520 vs Triton 5584 us, ratio 0.630) now includes the faster align, so it can only move further ON. The margin rules out a flip, so no rega-vs-Triton confound. If rega ft were OFF, the ft class is dead code (the Triton path keeps moe_align_block_size), and the ft PATH CHOSEN line would show it.

experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096: owns the low/high call site (_experts_rega). Gates at 0.649/0.651 and bit-identical align outputs mean rega's GEMM rows cannot shift through the change. Only the launch count changes (1 to 2 kernels), worth ~2-3 us of launch/tail overlap.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (carries moe-align-local-routes-parallel-port): defines _align_parallel, which is both the equivalence reference and the incumbent timed in the gate, and _align2_setup returns OFF unless align_par_ok. That is a precondition, not a confound. Check that align_par_ok is ON in the log.

experts-turn4-ssdq-s1b-dataptr-symbol-fix, experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn, sglang-pipeline-parity, experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: the ssdq and Marlin fallbacks keep _align_parallel byte-identical and are not the timed path at turn_1/turn_4 (rega wins those gates), so they do not interact.
interference: No companion. The change is one call site on one path, with outputs proven bit-identical in prepare, so every downstream kernel row should stay flat. The per-shape profile gives _align_parallel_kernel (master, 17/71/393-419 us) against _align2_count_kernel + _align2_place_kernel directly, and the re-printed per-class PATH CHOSEN line says which classes ran. A gain or a loss is therefore attributable from this one run. An ab-revert of the parent would remove the ft call site and with it the main expected gain. An ab-tune of chunk size is already covered by the in-prepare gate choosing between 512 and 1024. A control isolating the ft class from low/high would only split ~2-3% into finer pieces already visible per load row. With 2 prefill checks left today, spending one on a companion buys nothing the profile does not already show.
rules_flags: None blocking. Before submitting, verify that _align_dispatch reads only local_ids.shape[0] and state['align2_ok'] (a plain dict of ints, which survives deepcopy and _rega_copy_tree). Verify that the count table is torch.empty((cdiv(n, chunk), 32)), sized by shape, and that kernel_fn has no .item()/.cpu()/print/try.

'align2_ok' must be in REGA_STATE_KEYS. Otherwise _rega_replay_check's mini state silently falls back to _align_parallel, and the A/B/C copy and replay checks validate a different align than the one timed. Without the key this is a correctness-validation hole, not a rule break.
Gate decisions are made from synthetic routings in prepare (_ssdq_case / _align2_cases), never from judge inputs. That is allowed.
open_questions: Which chunk size wins the ft gate, and do the place kernel's regs or spills at CHUNK 1024 with NCH_P2 128 matter? Print the per-class medians next to master's ~393 us.

Does the single tail program (≈115k sentinel stores + 8222-entry block_experts at T=16384) stay under 10 us? If it falls back to the distributed fill, that form needs its own equivalence pass on the local-saturated and one-expert cases at T=16384.
d792's log tail lost the align2 lines. Confirm in the new log that the 16:low, 16:high and 16:ft classes are each ON, so that flat turn rows mean 'ran and did not help' and not 'never ran'.

Does the ft equivalence suite at T=16384 include 'one-expert' (all 131072 routes on expert 7: 8192 blocks for one expert) as well as 'local-saturated' (cap fully used, empty sentinel range)? Both extremes should be required.
